title: Governed deployment scorecard & traffic runbook
summary: Compact operational scorecard to drive go/no-go and traffic phasing decisions for model feature launches. Couples live telemetry thresholds with an owner-by-step traffic runbook and pre-mortem contingency actions. Intended as the canonical source in early rollouts and handoff to ops for scale.
objectives: Provide a single pane for readiness signals (latency, error-rate, cost/unit, quality regressions)
Map traffic percentages to operational actions and slack escalation points
Document explicit owner responsibilities for each phased step of a rollout
Tie automated alerts to measured thresholds and immediate mitigations

5xx rate|0.8%|0.3%|<1%|>2%|Rollback to previous model version and pause canary|SRE lead

traffic_runbook_steps: Step 0 — Prelaunch: Verify model pinning, rollout recipe, monitoring hooks, and canary environment matches prod traffic patterns
Step 1 — 1% traffic (probe): Observe for 30m steady-state; no SLO breaches and <0.5% error-rate delta before progressing
Step 2 — 5% traffic: Validate latency P95/P99 and cost delta; confirm KV cache warm-up; owner signoff required
Step 3 — 20% traffic: Run traffic-slice checks (region, tenant, heavy prompt shapes); enable additional tracing hooks
Step 4 — 50% traffic: Bring standby capacity online; confirm autoscale and dedicated pools if required
Step 5 — 100% traffic: Full cutover only after checklist completed and green signal from SRE and Applied ML
ownership_roster: Product-ops: runbook steward, traffic percentage gating decisions
SRE: infra health, latency and error SLIs, rollback authority
Serving-runtime: kernel selection and model-variant routing checks
Applied ML: quality metrics, eval set ownership, prompt/adapter remedies
Solutions Eng: customer-specific gating and VIP runway coordination
threshold_matrix_notes: Thresholds intentionally conservative for first two customers to validate assumptions
Alerting mapped to paged incidents for infra and to Slack ops channel for product-ops
Use short evaluation windows (5-15m) for early probe stages, extend to 1h at 20%+
Cost thresholds use rolling 24h averages to avoid transient spikes causing premature rollbacks
contingency_checklist: Immediate: Re-route 100% of canary traffic to baseline model (automated fallback)
Short term: Reduce traffic to previous stable bucket (5%) and keep investigation channel open
Medium term: Patch prompt or apply lightweight quantization profile if cost spike persists
Long term: Re-evaluate model architecture selection and batch strategy with Applied ML and Serving-runtime
communication_plan: Internal: Post incident summary in #prod-ops with root cause and timeline within 2 hours
Executive: Hourly status updates for first 6 hours when rollout is paused or rollbacked
Customers: Pre-approved message templates for impacted enterprise tenants; coordinate with CS
decisions_pending: Whether to require SRE signoff for 20% -> 50% transition for all public rollouts
Finalize the cost-per-token soft limit for early access customers
Approve default batching profile for latency-sensitive routes
retrospective_prompts: What signals missed early warning signs and why?
Were ownership handoffs clear and executed on time?
Which mitigations were fastest to reduce user impact?
Could monitoring thresholds be automated based on historical baselines?
notes: Working doc: expect edits. This sheet is intentionally action-first — keep rows short and link to detailed investigations in Confluence. For any candidate change to thresholds, create a short RFC and attach telemetry sample windows (last 72h) before applying in prod.
